archetype.name: Playoff Team (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A Cleveland side whose top-10 shooting and ball security carry it to a playoff-caliber margin, while a defense now in the bottom third keeps it from being more than that.

report.headline: A top-10 offense covering for a defense that keeps slipping
report.take:
Cleveland at 7-7 is exactly what its play says it is. The Net Rtg of 1.6 ranks 15th, the W vs Pt Diff of -1 says the margin implies 8 wins rather than 7, and the 82-game pace sits at 41 wins. No luck is propping this up and none is dragging it down. What has changed is the shape of the team. The offense is excellent: an ORtg of 117.8 (7th), an eFG % of 55.8 (4th) and a TOV % of 12 (4th). It now takes 46.9% of its shots from three, more than even the 64-win 2024-25 team's 45.7. The defense has a DRtg of 116.2, 20th in the league.

The engine is Donovan Mitchell: 5th on the shooting-guard tab, 299 points on a TS % of 60.6, a 28.6 usage and a team-best On-Off of +10.5 among regulars. Around him the efficiency is real. Tyrese Proctor has a TS % of 68.2 with a 2.9 BPM in a bench role. Jarrett Allen is at 69.0, and Evan Mobley (6th on his tab, 3.7 BPM) has anchored an A- frontcourt. The hole is on the wing. Peyton Watson has taken 310 minutes on a 44.0 TS % with a -5.0 BPM, the wings grade out a D, and the three listed wings have produced zero Win Shares combined.

The numbers hide where the defense actually breaks. The shot defense is fine: an Opp eFG % of 52.5 ranks 10th and an Opp Rim FG % of 62.4 ranks 6th. The problem is that Cleveland forces almost nothing. Its Opp TOV % of 11.0 is dead last, so opponents get a clean shot nearly every trip. The points leak through two spots. Shooting guards take 25.3% of opponents' points against a league norm of 22.4%. Opposing centers average 22.71 points and 16.36 rebounds, the most rebounds any defense allows to that position. The decline is not new either. Def Rank went from 1st in 2022-23 to 15th last year to 20th now. James Harden's On-Off of -18.9 next to Mitchell's +10.5 is a striking split, and it hints the non-Mitchell units are the soft spot, but 13 games of on-off is noisy.

The direction is mildly down. October came at 121 scored and 116 allowed a game. November has been 114.88 to 115.75, and the last five games run 3.6 points a game worse than even, a swing of -5.24 against the season. Now Mobley is listed Out. The schedule offers a soft landing: three straight at home and two of four against a Chicago team ranked 28th. This should still settle as a mid-40s win team that wins with offense, unless the defense finds a way to create turnovers.

strengths.title: Efficient, careful, three-heavy offense
strengths.body: Cleveland shoots well and rarely gives the ball away: an eFG % of 55.8 ranks 4th and a TOV % of 12 ranks 4th, adding up to a 117.8 ORtg. This is a repeat profile, not a hot start. The offense ranked 1st in 2024-25 and 6th last season with similar shooting. Expect it to hold in the top 8 even if the 37% from three cools a bit.

strengths.title: Mitchell drives the good minutes
strengths.body: Mitchell ranks 5th of 109 shooting guards. He carries a 28.6 usage at a 60.6 TS %, and the team is 10.5 points per 100 better with him on the floor. That impact is what turns a mediocre defense into a positive margin. It is sustainable as long as he stays healthy, and the team has no comparable creator behind him.

strengths.title: The rim is still protected
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 62.4% within four feet, 6th best and below the league's 65.1. Allen, finishing at a 69.0 TS % on the other end, is the constant here. It is the one defensive pillar left from the Def Rank 1 era.

concerns.title: A defense that forces nothing
concerns.body: Cleveland's Opp TOV % of 11.0 is last in the league, so even a respectable Opp eFG % produces a 20th-ranked DRtg. Opponents simply get more clean looks. This is a multi-year slide from a 1st-ranked defense in 2022-23, so it is structural, not early noise. Shooting guards and centers are where it shows most.

concerns.title: Mobley out thins the frontcourt
concerns.body: Mobley is listed Out after posting a 3.7 BPM, and he is the best two-way piece of the A- frontcourt. His minutes fall to Mario Hezonja (-1.2 BPM) and Thomas Bryant. That stretches a defense that already gives opposing centers the most rebounds in the league. How long he is out isn't in the sheet, which is the biggest unknown on this card.

concerns.title: No functional wing
concerns.body: The wings grade a D. Watson leads them in minutes with a 44.0 TS % and a -5.0 BPM, and the group's combined Win Shares are zero. Both Watson and Jaylon Tyson are day-to-day. Unless one of them finds a shot, this stays the weak link all year.

trend.note: A 4-2 October built on 121 points a game gave way to a 3-5 November in which Cleveland has been slightly outscored. The last five games run 5.24 points a game worse than the season margin.

weekAhead.headline: Three at home, two against Chicago: a chance to reset
weekAhead.body:
This is the softest week Cleveland is likely to see for a while. Chicago comes twice, ranked 28th with a 121.0 DRtg that also ranks 28th. Indiana is 22nd with an offense ranked 22nd. Three of the four games are at home, and the only real test is Memphis midweek. A 2-2 week would be a disappointment given the opposition.

The complication is Mobley's absence plus two day-to-day wings. The rotation will lean even harder on Mitchell and the guards. That fits Chicago, whose defense bleeds points to point guards and concedes the league's highest rim rate. It is riskier against Memphis, which shoots 39.2% from three and rebounds 29.7% of its misses.

keyMatchups.title: Feasting on Chicago's leaky defense
keyMatchups.body: Chicago allows the highest Opp Rim Rate in the league at 38.4% and gives point guards 29.42 points a game. That is a clear opening for Harden and Proctor to attack downhill and for Allen to finish. Two games against this defense should restore some of the October scoring.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis guards versus Cleveland's soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Memphis has an A backcourt and the 2nd-best 3P % in the league. Cleveland gives shooting guards a bigger share of its points than the league norm. On the other end, Memphis holds shooting guards to 21.69 points, among the stingiest in the league, which makes it a hard night for Mitchell. This is the game of the week to lose.

keyMatchups.title: Indiana offers the wings a chance
keyMatchups.body: Indiana's offense is 22nd and it rebounds a league-worst 21.5% of its own misses, so Cleveland's defense should hold up. Indiana also gives small forwards 28.14 points a game. If Watson or Tyson is ever going to have a productive night, this is it.

weekAhead.watch: How the Mobley-less frontcourt of Allen, Hezonja and Bryant handles the glass and the opposing center, above all against Memphis's offensive rebounding.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the sustainable part. Cleveland has posted top-8 offenses in three of the last four seasons with this shooting and ball-security profile, and Mitchell's efficiency is in line with his role. The defense is the question. A last-place Opp TOV % and a Def Rank that has slid for three straight years point to a team that will live around 20th unless the rim protection gets help on the perimeter. With a record that already matches its margin, there is no regression owed in either direction.

That adds up to a team in the 43-48 win range, a little better than the current 41-win pace once Mobley returns and the schedule evens out. The Net Rtg should settle somewhere between 2 and 5. That makes Cleveland a playoff team chasing Detroit in the Central rather than a contender, unless the wing spot or the turnover problem gets fixed.
swingFactors: Whether the defense can force any turnovers
A playable wing emerging from Watson or Tyson

confidence.note: 14 games, a record that matches its margin, but Mobley's injury timeline is unknown.
